core_obligations: Rewrite the constructed product as adjoint to the composite of the counit maps applied to Lf^* of the tensor of the two derived global sections (proof lines 7220-7229).

Translate the classes into maps xi: A[-i] to RGamma(X, K) and eta: A[-j] to RGamma(X, M), and record the shift-tensor identification that turns their tensor into a map from A[-i-j] (proof lines 7230-7251).

Identify the cup product as the map adjoint to the composite of the two counits applied to the pulled back tensor, and use epsilon_K Lf^*xi = xi-tilde and epsilon_M Lf^*eta = eta-tilde to conclude that the two adjoints coincide (proof lines 7252-7263).
proof_roadmap: Express the constructed product through the counit (proof lines 7220-7229).
Compare the two sides after the shift-tensor identification (proof lines 7230-7251).
Use the counit identities to conclude the agreement (proof lines 7252-7263).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the product on hypercohomology constructed just before it, as a map adjoint to the counit of the adjunction between Lf^* and Rf_* applied to the tensor product of the two derived global sections, agrees with the cup product (statement lines 7214-7217, with the construction in the preceding paragraph of the chapter). The proof unwinds both sides of the comparison: writing the classes as maps xi: A[-i] to RGamma(X, K) and eta: A[-j] to RGamma(X, M), the tensor xi tensor eta corresponds under a shift-tensor identification to a map out of A[-i-j], and the cup product is by definition the map adjoint to the composite of the counits applied to Lf^* of that tensor (proof lines 7219-7258). The agreement then follows from the two identities epsilon_K composed with Lf^*xi equals the map induced by xi, and similarly for eta, which give the identification of the two adjoints (proof lines 7259-7263). The claim is H2: a short adjunction computation, with the only hidden point being the sign absorbed by the shift convention, which the author isolates in a footnote.
